title: US defaults on debt by 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the United States federal government fails to make a scheduled payment on any Treasury note, bond, or bill at any point between November 5, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

If Standard & Poor’s, Moody’s, or Fitch publicly classify any U.S. sovereign debt as being in default during the qualifying period this will qualify for a “Yes” resolution. 

The resolution source will be official information from the U.S. Department of the Treasury, Standard & Poor’s, Moody’s, and Fitch.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent legislative action underpins trader confidence in no US default by 2027. The July 2025 One Big Beautiful Bill Act raised the debt ceiling by $5 trillion to $41.1 trillion, deferring the next binding limit until late winter or mid-summer 2027, with extraordinary measures likely extending Treasury runway into late 2027. Congress has repeatedly resolved prior debt limit impasses through raises or suspensions rather than permitting missed payments on obligations, preserving the dollar’s reserve status and Treasury market stability. While 2027 negotiations could involve partisan leverage, historical patterns and the systemic costs of any breach support the 96.9% implied probability for no default. Realistic scenarios that could alter odds include an unusually prolonged standoff delaying payments or unforeseen fiscal shocks narrowing the window before resolution.
